2026/10/06 | 12:08 AM » a reflection on dirk strider

i used to dislike the homestuck epilogues and hsbc. there were a couple of reasons why i did, including but not limited to feeling like i had to due to the people around me, but one of the primary ones was the direction dirk's character took.

dirk strider's character has been talked to death about online, but let's talk about him some more. i haven't read homestuck proper in a long time, so bear with me as i stumble around remembering canon characterizations versus the versions fandom has attached itself to.

one major cornerstone of canon dirk's characterization is his struggle with morality. he's someone who feels like he is an innately bad person. being surrounded by his splinters doesn't help, as he sees all of his bad qualities reflected right back at him. and his views of his other selves are almost always drenched in bad faith and low-expectations; he rarely has anything good to say about them/himself, and expects the worst behaviors from them. suffice to say, it's clear that he hates himself.

his conversation with dave lays things out pretty clearly, regarding dirk's thoughts about himself as a person:

DIRK: Right.
DIRK: The thing with that, with my adult self's...
DIRK: Ways.
DIRK: The sad thing is,
DIRK: I can really see it.
DIRK: How someone like me can go unchecked in life, and turn out to become a much worse person than I already am.

he already views himself as a toxic person who poisons innocent peoples' lives. being a "good person" is an active fight for him, something he has to work towards. you could argue that this is the same for anyone, but dirk in particular believes he is already a bad person inherently—that he has to be checked, has to regularly keep under control his worse traits, in order to be anything close to good. that without those checks and balances, it might as well be an inevitability that he turns out to be awful. he's fighting an uphill battle.

is his belief unfounded?

dirk's biggest issue that we see reflected across his splinters and alt selves is his need for control. it permeates his every action. he's someone who is used to having to take the initiative in order to survive, and simply sitting back and allowing things to play out doesn't exactly come naturally to him.

with a strong trust in his own judgement—something he has to have in order to take initiative—he has a tendency to view himself as the person who knows what needs to be done, how things need to be, in order for things to turn out well. in order to survive a game of life or death. this presents itself in how he interacts with his friends pre-game, attempting to push them towards what he views are better versions of themselves "for their own sakes". in short: he thought he knew what was best for them, better than they did, and took to trying to change things himself.

there is a foundation for toxic behaviors to take root in, a foundation he recognizes in himself. it's his fuckups that have made him so hyperaware of himself and his capacity to become a "bad person".

most important to outline is the fact that he hasn't given up, though.

DIRK: I guess I'm just relieved I still have some time to make sure that doesn't happen.

i'm going to talk a little about my feelings now, because this is my blog and i do what i want.

i saw a lot of myself in dirk. i didn't have his control issues or any real trust in my own judgement, but i connected deeply with the feeling of being inherently, innately bad, and hating myself for it. i always felt like something was just wrong with me and how i connected—or failed to connect—with people. and so i related heavily to this feeling of fighting an uphill battle against yourself in order to be a "good person". i took a lot of comfort in seeing a character who struggled with themself like this, like me. i projected a lot onto dirk strider.

so when the epilogues were released, and dirk became everything that he had feared he would become, it made me feel a certain way. i remember it feeling as if it were badly written fanfiction, and written specifically to upset as many people as possible.

it just felt awful for me personally to read. don't get me wrong, i love watching shit hit the fan just as much as any other angst fanfic reader likes, but it just felt like such a bleak outcome that left a bad taste in my mouth. as it turns out, i prefer happy endings when it comes to canon even if i enjoy a foray into the dark every once in a while. i was so invested in dirk's character, and desperately wanted to see him grow and heal as a person, as if to show to me that i myself wasn't a lost cause. and i wanted to see these characters who i'd grown up with get their happy ending after dealing with so much in the events of canon.

so in short, i disliked what post-canon did to dirk strider's character.

since then, my perspective has shifted a bit. my social environment has changed, and i've grown a lot more and started practicing actually thinking for myself for once.

i enjoy hard-earned happy endings, with emphasis on the hard-earned. i like things to get worse before they get better. i like to see characters get dragged through the mud and go through all of the ugliness that is recovery, healing, and personal growth. one example that comes to mind is steven universe future. i really enjoyed the depiction of CPTSD, and all of steven's unresolved trauma bubbling to the surface and being dragged out into the open once active and immediate issues of survival were finally over. i find great comfort in stories like that.

here's the thing with homestuck's post-canon: it isn't done yet.

i'd been viewing dirk's descent into becoming and embracing the role of the villain as his ending, with a sense of finality. but it clearly isn't going to be a one-dimensional story with a simple answer of "kill dirk strider", given everything we know about how homestuck handles narratives and meta, expectations and subversions. we're in the "it gets worse" part of the "it gets worse before it gets better". granted, it's much, much worse than the typical trauma and personal growth arc, but hsbc is pretty unique in that.

i feel like we don't get enough of characters in media who go through incredibly messy recoveries and personal growth. when i say messy, i mean messy—i mean hurting the people they love kind of messy. i mean not being a "perfect victim" kind of messy. looking at epilogues and hsbc dirk with this reframing, it's a lot more bearable to deal with.

of course, this all hinges on the idea of dirk being a part of hsbc's happy ending, assuming there even is one. it hinges on the idea that he still has room to grow, that he isn't too far gone. that can be a hard sell considering all that post-canon dirk has done and is currently doing. but a part of me can't help but hope that there's room for something like "redemption" in spite of it all. that dirk strider's story won't be that of a self-fulfilled prophecy of being doomed to be a horrible person. that maybe some version of dirk out there will get to live out a fulfilled and happy life in canon.

it's very possible that my hopes are naive, and that i should let go of it before i get burned. but i think i'll let myself hold onto some foolish scraps of hope for once.

that's about all i have to say on the matter of dirk strider in post-canon. i'm interested in seeing where the story of hsbc leads now with this reframing in mind. and even if dirk doesn't get a happy ending with everyone, even if he remains a villain who can't be redeemed, i can now more easily appreciate what the epilogues and hsbc have to offer relative to exploring characters and their worst selves. there's always the chance that hsbc just won't be the kind of story that i like to read, and that's okay too—it'd just mean it isn't for me.

maybe this will age terribly. that's also fine. i want to document my line of thought and see where things go. i want to become more comfortable expressing thoughts and feelings that have the risk of being "wrong". if anything, this blog post will serve as a preserved slice of time from before hsbc ends, and a piece of myself i can look back on to see how my thoughts have evolved.
